summary_of_change:
Texas Instruments is executing near peak cyclical efficiency across its manufacturing and distribution infrastructure. Over the trailing four quarters, quarterly revenue expanded from $4.15B in late 2025 to $5.46B in Q2 2026, translating to a current annualized run-rate of $21,852.0M (+23.0% YoY). Gross margins expanded sequentially from 56.8% to 61.4%, driven by rising 300mm fab utilization and direct catalog pricing adjustments on TI.com. Operating margins have rebounded sharply to 42.3%, demonstrating the operating leverage of internal 300mm wafer processing, which delivers a structural 40% unpackaged die-cost advantage over standard 200mm foundry peers.

Unit volume shipments across TI's 80,000+ catalog SKUs and 100,000+ global customer accounts have inflected positively, led by broad-market industrial channel replenishment, rising electronic content in automotive powertrains, and doubling demand for high-efficiency analog power management in AI data center server racks. Furthermore, modular capital expenditures have passed their cyclical peak, stepping down from an annual run-rate of $4.8B to $3.3B, which accelerated trailing twelve-month free cash flow to $6.53B.

Capital allocation remains focused on shareholder distributions and disciplined vertical scale. The company returned $5.8B to shareholders over the past year through its 22-year dividend growth record and selective buybacks, while announcing a $7.5B all-cash acquisition of Silicon Laboratories to consolidate low-power wireless IoT connectivity onto TI's 300mm manufacturing footprint. Total debt stands at $14.05B against $7.00B in cash ($7.05B net debt), with robust operating cash flows ($8.67B TTM) providing ample balance sheet liquidity.
